text:
Maya CS: quick weekly check-in for Tide Labs dedicated pool — noticed a sustained spike in GPU hours and queue depth overnight, potentially impacting their renewal. Can folks eyeball the metrics below and flag any immediate takedowns or enablement actions?

Raj Ops: on it. can you drop the last 24h numbers? any big jobs or onboarding bursts?

capacity-bot: snapshot for tenant=tide-labs (24h window)
```
/infra pool metrics --tenant tide-labs --window 24h
GPU_hours: 1420
saturation: 0.92
avg_queue_depth: 9
p95_latency_ms: 420
errors_percent: 0.8
estimated_spend_usd: 28400
```

Leo SRE: 92% saturation + avg queue 9 is rough. p95 420ms — we should protect critical routes. can we push their noncritical batch reranks to lower tier or delay by 30m? :thinking_face:

Olivia SE: tide-labs started a large recommender A/B this week, onboarding ramped faster than expected. I flagged the job tags as `recommender-ab` — we can coordinate with them to throttle experiments for the next 48h.

Raj Ops: noted. any signs of increased errors tied to model variant? could be cache misses or quantization fallback. @Kyle Runtime can you check workload labels?

Kyle Runtime: saw a few model-variant mismatches in the logs yesterday, rolled a runtime tweak last night that should reduce KV misses and lower p95 by ~30%. I'll attach a follow-up metric after the next hour.

Maya CS: thanks. big thing is renewal sensitivity — Tide's finance called out this spike in spend. proposed actions: 1) offer a one-time credit for the onboarding burst, 2) schedule an enablement workshop to tune batching/quantization suggestions, 3) short-term priority rules to keep user-facing routes green. Thoughts?

Leo SRE: agree. immediate stopgap = priority policy to route `user-facing` requests to dedicated fast lane, and throttle `recommender-ab` to spare capacity. I can push a policy change now.

Raj Ops: I'll queue a config to throttle tags `recommender-ab` to 25% concurrency until 2026-04-01 or manual release.

Olivia SE: I'll ping Tide and ask them to gate the big experiments while we stabilize. also prepping a short playbook for their engineers with concrete size/batch suggestions.

Maya CS: cool — can we confirm after the throttle and runtime tweak: p95, avg queue, and spend trend? if numbers improve, we offer the credit and keep renewal on track. I'll set a 30m follow-up thread. :thumbsup:

capacity-bot: scheduled follow-up metric check in 30m (1979999999 -> 1980000123)

Kyle Runtime: will post updated numbers in 20m.

Maya CS: thanks team — tagging this as high priority for Tide renewal.
